# Purpose of this document

This is the dated record of how the COSMIC cognitive harmonisation project decided to do what it is doing: each decision, the reason for it, and what it replaced. It is updated whenever a decision is made or reversed.

<div class="now">
**Where we are (24 Nov 2026).** This stage is a feasibility study of a new approach. Five pilot cohorts (MYHAT, Sydney MAS, KLOSCAD, HELIAD, SPAH) have been selected against stated criteria and curated at item level. A two-round Delphi will classify each cohort's tests into the five HCAP domains; deciding which items link cohorts is a separate step. HRS-HCAP is the reference for the common scale. An ethics application, which will also cover a comparison of AI and expert classification, is planned before Christmas.
</div>

<p class="key">
<span class="st decided">Decided</span> agreed by the project team
<span class="st done">Done</span> work completed
<span class="st proposed">Proposed</span> drafted, awaiting agreement
<span class="st open">Open</span> not yet addressed
<span class="st superseded">Superseded</span> replaced by a later decision
</p>

Companion documents: `documentation/harmonisation_strategy.md` (the strategy and its evidence), `documentation/delphi_protocol.md` (the Delphi in detail) and `documentation/item_mapping_conventions.md` (how items are coded).

# How the strategy has changed

The strategy changed several times between September and November 2026. Each change had a reason, and the current plan keeps something from every stage.

<div class="timeline">

<div class="tl">
<span class="when">Sep 2026</span> · <span class="what">Original plan: Delphi first, domain scores, then global cognition</span><br>
<span class="why">All COSMIC cohorts. A modified Delphi would classify each test into HCAP domains, followed by domain scores and a global score.</span><br>
<em>Kept:</em> HCAP as the framework; the Delphi; the separation of "what does it measure" from "can it link cohorts".
</div>

<div class="tl">
<span class="when">Oct 2026 (by 19 Oct; exact date to confirm)</span> · <span class="what">After consulting Alden Gross (HCAP): item-level curation first, pilot in English-speaking cohorts</span><br>
<span class="why">The hard part is deciding which items can link studies, not fitting the model. That needs item-level review of how each test was given and scored. A pilot in English-speaking cohorts (MAS, PATH, EAS, MYHAT) would reduce language and cultural confounding.</span><br>
<em>Kept:</em> item-level curation in HCAP's layout. <em>Dropped on 3 Nov:</em> the restriction to English-speaking cohorts.
</div>

<div class="tl">
<span class="when">22 Oct 2026</span> · <span class="what">Scope discussion: the aim is the whole consortium</span><br>
<span class="why">The project lead restated the aim of covering all COSMIC cohorts, accepting that the output need not be perfect. A two-track plan was suggested: broad curation across the consortium alongside intensive method development in a small pilot.</span><br>
<em>Status:</em> the two-track plan was a suggestion and was never formally adopted. The current plan (pilot, then scale up in batches) serves the same purpose.
</div>

<div class="tl">
<span class="when">Late Oct to early Nov 2026 (date to confirm)</span> · <span class="what">Considered a norm-based categorical index</span><br>
<span class="why">After meeting Karen Blackmon: the International Brain Health Index needs only domain mapping and local norms, which suits low- and middle-income settings. It gives categories, not scores, and was unpublished.</span><br>
<em>Status:</em> not adopted. Could complement co-calibration later.
</div>

<div class="tl">
<span class="when">3 Nov 2026</span> · <span class="what">Custodian-led mapping</span><br>
<span class="why">Each cohort's custodian would map their own tests to HCAP domains using a pre-filled questionnaire, with a later check by neuropsychologists. Reasons: custodians know their data, and it respects local context. The restriction to English-speaking cohorts was dropped the same day. An independent review that day added that mapping alone does not harmonise scores, so a statistical method had to be chosen as well.</span><br>
<em>Kept:</em> inclusion of diverse cohorts from the start; cohorts checking our work. <em>Dropped on 4 Nov:</em> dependence on cohorts replying.
</div>

<div class="tl">
<span class="when">4 Nov 2026</span> · <span class="what">Expert-panel Delphi, cohort input optional</span><br>
<span class="why">Cohort response rates are falling and many older studies have no staff to reply. Decision: return to a Delphi with a panel as diverse as possible. Cohorts are asked to confirm, and silence is not a blocker. The "culturally similar or different" grouping was dropped, because differences belong to each cohort's version of a test, not to regions. Measures or cohorts that cannot be agreed are left out.</span>
</div>

<div class="tl">
<span class="when">13 to 15 Nov 2026</span> · <span class="what">Method aligned with HCAP's published procedure</span><br>
<span class="why">The questionnaire was rebuilt in REDCap and its link question changed to HCAP's three categories (confident, tentative, none), so decisions are comparable with HCAP's. A draft protocol proposed two-rater review of everything, with the Delphi panel reserved for the hard cases.</span><br>
<em>Kept:</em> REDCap, one test per page with a reference panel. <em>Dropped on 24 Nov:</em> linking questions in the Delphi.
</div>

<div class="tl">
<span class="when">19 Nov 2026</span> · <span class="what">Feasibility framing; cohort choice must be justified</span><br>
<span class="why">The pilot is to be presented as a feasibility study of a new approach. The choice of cohorts needed an explicit rationale, with Europe and Oceania, different languages and good coverage of the HCAP domains. Which cohorts are included will not depend on whether their investigators join the panel. Every panellist will rate every test.</span>
</div>

<div class="tl current">
<span class="when">23 Nov 2026</span> · <span class="what">Pilot cohorts selected against stated criteria</span><br>
<span class="why">Purposive, maximum-variation selection. Eligible cohorts have item- or subtest-level data, cover at least four of the five HCAP domains, and share at least three candidate linking items. Selected: MYHAT (USA), Sydney MAS (Australia), KLOSCAD (South Korea), HELIAD (Greece) and SPAH (Brazil). MYNAH and Uganda move to the first expansion batch.</span>
</div>

<div class="tl current">
<span class="when">24 Nov 2026</span> · <span class="what">Delphi narrowed to domain classification; HRS-HCAP as reference; AI comparison planned</span><br>
<span class="why">Panel experts cannot judge linking unless they hold the data, so the Delphi asks only which HCAP domain each test measures, with confidence and any second domain, over two rounds without discussion. Linking is decided separately. HRS-HCAP sets the common scale. Comparing AI classification with the expert panel is planned as a contribution to the field, subject to ethics approval.</span>
</div>

# Current method {.tabset}

## Pipeline

| Stage | What happens | Status |
|:--|:--|:-:|
| 1. Inventory | List cognitive variables in each cohort's files (names and labels only) | <span class="st done">Done for pilot</span> |
| 2. Item-level curation | One row per item per cohort in HCAP's layout; proposed links flagged | <span class="st done">Draft v0.3</span> |
| 3. Delphi: domain classification | Panel assigns each test to an HCAP domain; two rounds | <span class="st proposed">In preparation</span> |
| 4. Linking decisions and cohort check | Project team proposes links from HCAP precedents; cohorts confirm test descriptions | <span class="st open">Not started</span> |
| 5. Linkage map | Check the cohorts can be connected, per domain | <span class="st open">Not started</span> |
| 6. Co-calibration | Factor / IRT models with linking items held equal | <span class="st open">Not started</span> |
| 7. Bias testing and validation | Targeted tests on tentative links | <span class="st open">Not started</span> |
| 8. Scale up | Add cohorts in batches | <span class="st open">Not started</span> |

**Pilot cohorts** (selected 23 Nov 2026): MYHAT (USA), Sydney MAS (Australia), KLOSCAD (South Korea), HELIAD (Greece), SPAH (Brazil).

**Selection criteria.** Purposive, maximum-variation sampling for a feasibility study.

- *Eligibility:* item- or subtest-level data available to the project; at least four of the five HCAP domains covered, including memory; at least three candidate linking items with HRS-HCAP or another eligible cohort.
- *Variation sought across the set:* continent; language and script; education and literacy; type of battery (full neuropsychological, CERAD, 10/66 screening).

| Cohort | Country, language | Battery | What it tests |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| MYHAT | USA, English | Full neuropsychological | Closest to HRS-HCAP; the hub that links the others |
| Sydney MAS | Australia, English | Full neuropsychological | Best case with MYHAT: same language, different continent |
| KLOSCAD | South Korea, Korean | CERAD | Non-Latin script; standardised battery; bridge to Korea's HCAP study |
| HELIAD | Greece, Greek | Full neuropsychological | Greek alphabet; many participants with little schooling |
| SPAH | Brazil, Portuguese | 10/66 screening | Low literacy; screening-only battery typical of LMIC cohorts |

*Limitations:* no African or South Asian cohort met the domain criterion (MYNAH and Uganda are in the first expansion batch); data access shaped eligibility; two cohorts are English-speaking; HELIAD and KLOSCAD link mainly through Trail Making and the MMSE total. MAS is included subject to data access; CLAS (China) is the substitute if access is delayed.

## Principles

1. **The unit is the test as given in a particular cohort.** Language, materials, timing and scoring are part of the item.
2. **Domain and linking are separate questions.** A test can measure memory and still be too different from another memory test to link cohorts.
3. **Experts classify; statistics test.** The Delphi panel assigns tests to domains. The project team proposes links (confident, tentative, none) from HCAP precedents, and tentative links are tested for bias before use.
4. **Links between COSMIC cohorts count as much as links to HRS-HCAP.** A US study is a poor only reference for many cohorts.
5. **Cohorts confirm; they are not a dependency.** No reply by the deadline means we proceed and mark the description unconfirmed.
6. **Uncertainty is recorded.** Vote counts, confidence, unconfirmed details and unresolved items are all kept.
7. **Not every cohort gets every score.** What cannot be linked defensibly is left out.
8. **Standardising within cohorts is not harmonisation.** Z-scores do not put cohorts on a common scale.

## Item curation

- Layout and codes follow HCAP's pre-statistical resource. An item that looks equivalent to an HCAP item takes HCAP's code and is flagged as a proposed link. Other items take a COSMIC code (`c###`).
- Linking confidence follows HCAP: 2 confident, 1 tentative, −1 the HCAP item is not in HRS-HCAP.
- v0.3 (23 Nov 2026): five pilot cohorts, 129 rows, 104 codes, 43 of them HCAP codes. 17 codes appear in two or more cohorts.
- Source variables for MYHAT, KLOSCAD, HELIAD and SPAH were checked against the cohort file headers; three rows remain flagged. MAS rows are drafted from the published baseline battery (Sachdev et al., 2010) until its data dictionary is available.

Workbook: `curation/COSMIC_Item_Mapping_Pilot_v0.3.xlsx`.

## Expert judgement

**Purpose of the Delphi** (agreed 24 Nov 2026): to agree which of the five HCAP domains each cohort's test measures. Linking is not asked of the panel, because experts cannot judge it without knowing the cohort's data.

**Questions asked for each test**

| # | Question | Response | Feeds |
|:-:|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | Which HCAP domain does this test mainly measure? | Orientation; memory; executive function / attention; language / fluency; visuospatial; cannot assign | Which domain factor the item loads on |
| 2 | How confident are you? | 3-point scale | Weight given to borderline decisions |
| 3 | Does it also measure a second domain? | One of the five domains, or none | Items measuring several domains are used for global cognition only |

- A context section opens the questionnaire: HCAP, its five domains, and what the panel is for.
- Panellists are asked not to use AI tools when answering.
- Two rounds, no discussion. Round 2 shows each panellist the group's answers beside their own.
- Every panellist rates every test.

**Panel.** A diverse panel of neuropsychologists, psychometricians and people who know the cohorts. Investigators of the five pilot cohorts are invited through COSMIC; if they decline, the pilot proceeds without them. Project team members do not rate. Candidates are not listed here until they have been invited.

**Consensus rule** <span class="st proposed">Proposed</span>: 75% agreement on the main domain. Items without consensus after Round 2 are used for global cognition only.

**Linking decisions** are made separately by the project team, using HCAP's precedents in the mapping workbook and the cohorts' confirmation of how tests were given.

**AI comparison** <span class="st proposed">Proposed</span>: an approved AI tool classifies the same test descriptions, with the method fixed in advance, and its classifications are compared with the panel's consensus and with HCAP's existing classifications. Requires a new ethics application.

Full protocol: `documentation/delphi_protocol.md` (to be revised to match these decisions).

## Statistical plan

Not yet started. The intended approach follows Gross et al. (2023):

- Confirmatory factor models (equivalent to item response theory models), fitted cohort by cohort, with linking-item parameters held equal across cohorts.
- Non-linking items stay in the model with their own parameters.
- Linking items are tested for bias; those with salient bias are demoted to non-linking.
- A global cognition factor first <span class="st proposed">Proposed</span>, then domain factors where a cohort has enough linked items.

**Reference:** HRS-HCAP <span class="st decided">Decided</span> 24 Nov 2026. Its item parameters are fixed first and COSMIC cohorts are placed on its scale through shared items, so COSMIC scores can be compared with HCAP's published results.

Still to decide: the minimum number of links per cohort, software, and how cohorts with only total scores are handled.

# Open decisions

**Before Round 1 of the Delphi**

- Agree the consensus threshold (proposed 75%).
- Confirm the panel's size and composition.
- Submit the ethics application before Christmas.
- Fix the AI comparison method: tool, prompt and number of runs.
- What panellists are offered (authorship or acknowledgement).
- Whether to register the protocol before Round 1.
- MAS data access; otherwise substitute CLAS.

**Before modelling**

- First target score: global cognition (proposed) or domains.
- Obtain HRS-HCAP data, and ask the HCAP team whether its item parameters can be shared.
- Minimum number of links for a cohort to be placed on the common scale.
- How cohorts with only total scores are handled.
- Bias-testing thresholds (proposed: those in Gross et al., 2023).
- Software.

**Data**

- Outstanding questions on individual cohorts are listed in the `Open_questions` tab of the mapping workbook.
- Cohort data requests are tracked in `cohort_tracking/Cohort review.xlsx`.

# Earlier designs {.tabset}

Kept for the record. None of these is current.

## Original Delphi (Sep 2026)

- About 14 experts would rate every test against five HCAP domains on a 1 to 5 scale (1 not assessed, 5 core), then name a primary domain and give a confidence rating.
- Round 2 would show each expert the anonymised panel summary and let them revise.
- Consensus: 75% naming the same primary domain.
- Linking suitability would be assessed separately as high-confidence, tentative or not suitable.

*Replaced on 15 Nov 2026* by the lighter questionnaire described above. The 75% threshold and the separation of domain from linking carried over.

## English-speaking pilot (Oct 2026)

- Shortlist: MAS, PATH, EAS and MYHAT. CSHA and WHICAP excluded as multilingual.
- Purpose: a proof of concept with less language and cultural confounding.

*Dropped on 3 Nov 2026.* MYHAT remains in the current pilot. MAS and PATH will be added when data access is approved.

## Questionnaire v2 (15 Nov 2026)

- Six domains (attention / processing speed separate from executive function), with definitions.
- Questions: main domain; other domains; confidence 1 to 5; what else might affect scores; link to one or more comparison items (confident, tentative, none) and what differs.
- Two raters to review everything, with the panel for hard cases.

*Replaced on 24 Nov 2026* by domain classification only, using the five HCAP domains.

## Custodian-led mapping (3 Nov 2026)

- Each cohort's custodian would receive a questionnaire pre-filled from their data dictionary and map their own tests to HCAP domains with a confidence rating.
- A second round would have neuropsychologists or an expert panel check the mappings.
- Incentives: co-authorship, visibility of the cohort's data, involvement in later projects.

*Replaced on 4 Nov 2026.* The cohort check in the current pipeline is the part that survived.

# References

- Gross AL, Li C, Briceño EM, Arce Rentería M, et al. Harmonisation of later-life cognitive function across national contexts: results from the Harmonized Cognitive Assessment Protocols. *Lancet Healthy Longevity* 2023;4(10):e573–e583.
- Briceño EM, Arce Rentería M, Gross AL, Jones RN, et al. A cultural neuropsychological approach to harmonization of cognitive data across culturally and linguistically diverse older adult populations. *Neuropsychology* 2023;37(3):247–257.
